rationale: Evidence: every iteration-0 trial went off track on all three development tracks (60/60, 0 finishes). Progress stalled at 0.10 to 0.14, and max_error reached 0.062 to 0.064, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Line-loss events were 1.0 in every trial, so the robot lost the tape early and never recovered. RMS error was only 0.026 to 0.030, and steering oscillation was low (0.08 to 0.14). That pattern points to a stiffness and speed problem rather than jitter. The robot drifts out to the limit under the 1.6 base speed and the kp of 2.5. The motor mismatch (about 2 percent) also adds a steady bias that kp alone does not remove. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 to 1.4, so the robot can hold the line through bends and the sensors can keep up. (2) kp 2.5 to 3.5, for a firmer correction at the edge of the tape. (3) kd 0.15 to 0.3, to damp the larger kp and avoid oscillation. (4) ki 0.0 to 0.1, a small integral term to cancel the steady motor-mismatch bias, kept small so it does not wind up. (5) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, so the sensors see a smoother, wider signal near the line edge, and line loss is less likely. The sensor geometry and sensor_weights are otherwise unchanged. Expected: fewer off-track ends, max_error below 0.05, and at least some finishes on the oval and s-bend. Completion time may be near 3 s, so base_speed is the next lever if the run is clean. Hypotheses to check next race: (a) line_loss_events drops to 0 or near 0; (b) steering_oscillation stays under about 0.15 with kd 0.3; (c) completion_time falls under 3 s at base_speed 1.4. If the robot still leaves the line, the next step is to move the sensors closer to the axle or reduce base_speed to 1.2.
